what: The theme of learning from natural teachers: Bodhya's six teachers (Piṅgalā, osprey, snake, bee, arrow-maker, maiden) all reappear among the avadhūta's twenty-four; Piṅgalā's song and maxim recur.
era: between the Mahābhārata's Śāntiparvan and the Bhāgavata (scholarly)

evidence.detail: the tradition treats both as Vyāsa's

what: The list of the sage's qualities of Bhāgavata 11.11.29-31 is reproduced nearly verbatim in Avadhūta Gītā 8.2-4.

evidence.detail: direction assumed from the Bhāgavata to the Avadhūta Gītā (U06 judgement, moderate)

what: The Bhagavad Gītā's form — a god teaching a hero/king, vibhūti and viśvarūpa chapters, field-and-knower and three-guṇa chapters — is taken over by the Īśvara, Devī, Śiva and Gaṇeśa Gītās (the Gaṇeśa Gītā reworks many verses with Gaṇeśa as the Lord).
era: first and early second millennium CE (scholarly)

evidence.detail: viśvarūpa: Devī Gītā 7.33, Śiva Gītā 7, Gaṇeśa Gītā 8; Śiva's dance vision in Īśvara Gītā 2.5
the later Gītās are widely read as sectarian responses to the Bhagavad Gītā

what: The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha's seven stages of knowledge (and stages of ignorance) and many of its verses appear in minor Upaniṣads such as the Varāha, Akṣi and Mahā Upaniṣads.

evidence.detail: the seven bhūmikās with the same names (recalled; to be verified by U04)
the tradition regards the Upaniṣads as śruti and prior
scholars generally take these Upaniṣads to borrow from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

what: Shared vocabulary (spanda, cit, the three spaces, the world as the shining of consciousness) between the Kashmiri Mokṣopāya/Yoga Vāsiṣṭha and Kashmir Śaiva texts; the only commentator on the Mokṣopāya, Bhāskarakaṇṭha, was a Śaiva.

evidence.detail: the Halle editors hold the Mokṣopāya to be independent of Śaiva theology; others see Śaiva influence

what: The Yoga Vāsiṣṭha names the Vijñānavādins and Śūnyavādins, allows the supreme state to be described in terms of no-self and emptiness, and declares the doctrines of external objects and of consciousness to be one for itself.

evidence.detail: scholars have long debated Buddhist influence on the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha

what: Tulsīdās's Rāmcaritmānas draws on the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa: the Śiva-Pārvatī frame, Rāma as Brahman with Sītā as his power, the nine means of devotion to Śabarī, Lakṣmaṇa's consolation of Guha.

evidence.detail: AR 3.10.22-27 and RCM Araṇyakāṇḍa (Śabarī); AR Ayodhyā and RCM Ayodhyā 92-93 (Lakṣmaṇa and Guha)

what: Eknāth's Marathi Eknāthī Bhāgavata makes the Uddhava Gītā (Bhāgavata Book 11) a central scripture of the Vārkarī tradition.
